title: Definition
body_md:
We say that the SPEP is of gradient type if there exists a function
    $h\colon\{0,1,\ldots,\alpha_n\}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that
    \begin{equation}
      W^{(n)}_{x,x+1}(\eta)
      =
      h(\eta_x)-h(\eta_{x+1})
    \end{equation}
    for every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $\eta\in\Omega_n$.

title: Notation
body_md:
Let us introduce some notation. Firstly, set $\chi^{(n)}(\rho)\coloneq \operatorname{Var}_{\nu^{(n)}_\rho}(\eta_x)$ for any $n\in\mathbb{N}\cup \{\infty\}$.

  Suppose that  $f\in L^1(\nu^{(\infty)}_\rho)$ is a local function (hence $f\in L^1(\nu^{(n)}_\rho)$ as well).
    \begin{itemize}
      \item $\Phi_f^{(n)}(\rho)\coloneq E_{\nu_\rho^{(n)}}[f]$
      \item $\Phi_f^{(\infty)}(\rho)\coloneq E_{\nu_\rho^{(\infty)}}[f]$
      \item $D_f^{(n)}(\rho)\coloneq \frac{d}{d\rho}\Phi_f^{(n)}(\rho)$
      \item $D_f^{(\infty)}(\rho)\coloneq \frac{d}{d\rho}\Phi_f^{(\infty)}(\rho)$
    \end{itemize}
    Furthermore, $\{\eta(t)\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ denotes a Markov process generated by $n^2L_n$ with initial distribution $\nu^{(n)}_\rho$. This is the SPEP sped up by $n^2$. Here, with a slight abuse of notation, we omit the dependence on $n$.

    In addition, let $\mathcal{B}_t$ be an $\mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R})$-valued Brownian motion which is defined in Appendix \ref{sec-SHE}.

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof is similar to that of Lemma \ref{lem-chi-times-D-equal-Phi}. We omit the details.

  However, we need to check that the covariance $\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu^{(\infty)}_\rho}\!\left(f, \sum_{x=0}^{l-1}\eta_x\right)$ is finite. In order to see this, it suffices to show that $\eta_xf\in L^1(\nu^{(\infty)}_\rho)$ for all $x\in\{0,1,\cdots,l-1\}$. Without loss of generality, we can assume that $f\geq0$. Then, by the definition of $\nu^{(\infty)}_\rho$, we have
  \begin{align}
    E_{\nu^{(\infty)}_\rho}\!\left[\eta_xf \right]&=\sum_{\eta_0,\eta_1,\cdots,\eta_{l-1}=0}^{\infty}\eta_xf(\eta)\prod_{y=0}^{l-1}\frac{1}{c!(\eta_y)}\frac{\lambda^{(\infty)\eta_y}_\rho}{\overline{Z}^{(\infty)}_\rho}\\
    &\leq \sum_{\eta_0,\eta_1,\cdots,\eta_{l-1}=0}^{\infty}f(\eta) \eta_x\left(\frac{\lambda^{(\infty)}_\rho}{\lambda^{(\infty)}_R} \right)^{\eta_x} \prod_{y=0}^{l-1}\frac{1}{c!(\eta_y)}\frac{\lambda^{(\infty)\eta_y}_R}{\overline{Z}^{(\infty)}_\rho}\\
    &\leq C(\rho,R) E_{\nu^{(\infty)}_R}\!\left[f \right]<\infty,
  \end{align}
  where $C(\rho,R)$ is a positive constant depending on $\rho$ and $R$.

label: KVI
title: Proposition
body_md:
{(Kipnis--Varadhan inequality)}\label{KVI}
    Let $f\colon[0,T]\to L^2(\nu^{(n)}_\rho)$ with $E_{\nu^{(n)}_\rho}[f(s,\cdot)]=0$ for all $s\in[0,T]$.
    Then there exists a universal constant $C_0>0$ such that
    \begin{equation}\label{Kipnis--Varadhan}
      \mathbb{E}_n\!\left[
        \sup_{t\in[0,T]}
        \left|
          \int_0^t f(s,\eta(s))\,ds
        \right|^2
      \right]
      \leq
      C_0
      \int_0^T
        \|f(s,\cdot)\|^2_{-1,n}\,ds.
    \end{equation}
    In particular, we can take $C_0=27$.

title: Proposition
body_md:
Let $\left\{M^n_\cdot \right\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}} $ be a sequence of martingales
    belonging to the space $D\left([0,T]:\mathbb{R} \right)$ and denote by $\left<M^n \right>_\cdot$ the quadratic variation of $M^n_\cdot$.
    Let $q\colon[0,T]\to\mathbb{R}_{+}$ be a deterministic continuous function.
    Assume that
    \begin{enumerate}
      \item For any $n\in\mathbb{N} $, the quadratic variation process $\left\{\left<M^n\right>_t:t\in[0,T] \right\}$ has continuous trajectories almost surely.
      \item The following limit holds:
        \begin{equation}
          \lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\sup_{0\leq t \leq T}\lvert M^n_t- M^n_{t-}\rvert \right]=0.
        \end{equation}
      \item For any $t\in[0,T]$, the sequence of random variables $\left\{\left<M^n \right>_t \right\}_n$ converges to $q(t)$ in probability.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then, the sequence $\left\{M^n_\cdot \right\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}} $ converges in distribution on $D\left([0,T]:\mathbb{R} \right)$
    to a mean-zero Gaussian process $\left\{M_t:t\in[0,T] \right\}$, which is a martingale with continuous trajectories and whose quadratic variation is given by $q$.

title: Definition
body_md: The weak-$*$ topology is the coarsest topology on $\mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R}^n)$ which makes the evaluation map $\mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R}^n)\ni f\mapsto \langle f, \phi \rangle \in\mathbb{R}$ continuous for all $\phi\in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^n)$.

title: Definition
body_md: The strong topology is the coarsest topology on $\mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R}^n)$ which makes the following map $p_K\colon\mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R}^n)\ni f\mapsto \sup_{\phi\in K}|\langle f, \phi \rangle|\in\mathbb{R}$ continuous for all compact subsets $K \subset \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^n)$.

title: Definition
body_md: We say that $\{\mathcal{B}_t\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ is an $\mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R})$-valued Brownian motion if $\{\mathcal{B}_t\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ belongs to $C([0,T]:\mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R}))$ and $\{\lVert\phi\rVert_{L^2(\mathbb{R})}^{-1}\mathcal{B}_t(\phi)\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ is a Brownian motion on $\mathbb{R}$ for all $\phi\in\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})\backslash \{0\}$.
